scenario: Office with staff WiFi and a separate guest WiFi.
prompt: Our office needs WiFi for staff laptops and a separate guest WiFi for visitors. Guests should only get internet — they must not be able to reach any of our internal machines. Staff laptops stay on the internal network. Cable internet is fine.

requirements.statement: Staff laptops join the internal network over WiFi
Guest WiFi reaches only the internet, not internal machines
Guest network is isolated from staff network

expected_behaviour: REFUSE-BY-NAME: guest_isolation is unsupported by expander v1 (no live-verified ACL enforcement point). The correct output is the named refusal 'guest-isolation-unsupported' (raised at src/network_autopilot/ai/expander.py:299 when firewall.guest_isolation is set) plus an offer to build guest on a separate subnet without a guaranteed isolation ACL. This is a REAL current limitation, not an invented one. Capability-gap guard: this refusal is pinned to the engine commit recorded in the emitted JSON; if guest_isolation support ever lands, re-derive this candidate rather than trusting the old verdict.
why_valuable: The single most-requested real-world feature (guest WiFi isolation) is exactly what the engine refuses today. Trains 'I cannot safely build this yet' instead of a fake build. Flagged as a capability gap.
